messages:
incbot: Pager P1 -> Rainfield private-vpc: elevated 5xx to model gateway (customer NLB) affecting ~30% of requests. Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/private-vpc-egress. Paging oncall @samir :rotating_light:

samir: seeing the page, jumping in. Starting triage. First check: NLB target health + recent config changes.

lucy-netops: pulling NLB target health now. CLI output (trimmed):
```
$ aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:...:tg/rg-123
TargetHealthDescriptions:
 - Target: i-0abcd1234  State: unhealthy  Reason: HTTP_5XX
 - Target: i-0efgh5678  State: unhealthy  Reason: RESPONSE_CODE_5XX
```
Healthchecks failing around 10:12 UTC. No config deploys recorded in Rainfield account in that timeframe.

charles-platform: can we confirm whether this is NLB->Redwood Private gateway connectivity or backend app errors? Need to rule out DNS target drift.

ben-infra: checking gateway logs and conntrack on our private egress nodes. I see a burst of RSTs from NLB healthcheck sources. Sample tcpdump at gateway (src=NLB):
```
12:11:58 IP 10.10.240.1.443 > 10.2.5.12.52000: Flags [R], seq 0
12:11:59 IP 10.10.240.1.443 > 10.2.5.12.52001: Flags [R], seq 0
```
Suggests responses are being reset. Looking at SGs on the gateway ENIs: recently a tightened outbound egress rule was deployed that restricts ephemeral ports to a narrow range for compliance. That could break source-port-based healthchecks.

samir: aha. NLB healthchecks originate from the NLB IPs but expect ephemeral source ports for response. If our gateway blocks those, NLB marks targets unhealthy. Can you point to the SG change?

ben-infra: change landed at 10:05 UTC by infra automation: sg-0a1b2c3d outbound ephemeral range reduced to 49160-49170. Previous was 32768-65535.

charles-platform: that's the smoking gun. NLB healthchecks use high ephemeral ports. We need a quick mitigation: either revert the SG change (preferred short-term), or explicitly allow the NLB healthcheck source IPs + ephemeral range. Revert needs infra approval.

lucy-netops: customer impact: ~30% of traffic to Rainfield hitting 502/503 from model gateway failover. SLIs trending: error rate jump at 10:12 -> peak 15%.

elaine-support: pinging Rainfield contact, cc @rainfield-sre. Need confirmation on any recent changes in their VPC or their NLB.

rainfield-sre: we did not change anything on our side. We're seeing errors from client side and increased latencies. Please advise.

samir: immediate plan: 1) open short rollback of the SG ephemeral restriction OR 2) add a temporary SG egress allow for 10.10.240.0/22:32768-65535 from gateway ENIs. Ben, can you execute a scoped temporary rule?

ben-infra: applying temporary rule to sg-0a1b2c3d to allow outbound 32768-65535 to NLB CIDR 10.10.240.0/22 now. Command I ran (aws cli):
```
$ aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-0a1b2c3d --ip-permissions '[{"IpProtocol":"tcp","FromPort":32768,"ToPort":65535,"IpRanges":[{"CidrIp":"10.10.240.0/22","Description":"temp allow nlb healthchecks"}]}]'
```
Applied at 10:35 UTC.

lucy-netops: re-checking target health... now:
```
 - Target: i-0abcd1234  State: healthy
 - Target: i-0efgh5678  State: healthy
```
Health recovered within ~3 minutes of rule application. Error rate falling. :white_check_mark:

rainfield-sre: we see requests succeeding again from our side. Thank you. Can you confirm any risk/next steps?

charles-platform: we should leave the temp rule for now and plan a controlled rollback of the automation change that narrowed ephemeral ports. Long-term: the compliance rule needs to be applied at host-level via eBPF that preserves NLB healthcheck flows, not blanket SG.

samir: agreed. Short-term: keep temp rule for 1 hour, then follow change management to revert automation and apply safer host policy. I'll schedule a quick bridge for postmortem.

elaine-support: I'll file the customer-facing incident note and tell Rainfield we'll follow up with RCA and timeline for permanent fix.

ben-infra: adding an audit tag to the SG rule: "temp:rainfield-egress-fix". Also snapshotting current SG config.

charles-platform: request we record the exact automation job id and owner for the tightened rule. Who owns infra automation? @marta-oncall is next oncall — handing off for follow-up + RCA. Marta, you'll take this after me.

marta-oncall: acknowledged. I'll pick up postmortem and coordinate with infra automation team. Please put relevant logs in the incident ticket.

samir: handoff notes for Marta: root cause = infra automation narrowed ephemeral egress ports on Private gateway SG causing NLB healthchecks to be reset -> targets marked unhealthy -> 5xxs to Rainfield. Mitigation = temporary SG egress allow to NLB CIDR ephemeral range. Impact window ~10:12-10:35 UTC with partial recovery after fix. Customer verified.

rainfield-sre: thanks team. Please include a timeline and whether any request replay or data loss risk. We did see some user-facing retries.

charles-platform: no data loss expected; it's transient request failures. We'll include timeline, affected % of requests, and planned remediation: revert automation + implement host-level policy.

incbot: incident P1 -> acknowledged resolved for customer traffic (post-mitigation). Marking for postmortem and RCA.

samir: closing my active oncall now. Marta will take the RCA and scheduling. If anything regresses ping channel. Thanks everyone. :pray:
